Subject: Hosting zones & keystore escrow — Ellipsis Health

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we scope our pilot, our security team has two immediate asks so we can complete the vendor review:

1) A short, signed confirmation of what hosting zones Redwood can commit to for a single-tenant private deployment (we need EU-only placement for PHI processing).
2) A concise operator-keystore custody statement and the instructions you use when escrow/hand-off is required for an on-prem HSM operator scenario (we're evaluating an HSM partner).

Practically — can you provide a minimal CAIQ/SIG excerpt or runbook pages that show (a) where tenant keys are stored by default, (b) how operator access is provisioned and audited, and (c) the steps you take when we request sealed escrow to a third-party HSM?

If possible, please include any filename stubs for evidence artifacts (runbook, inventory, signed statement). We can treat these as sensitive artifacts in our VDR.

Can we aim to get this before our internal risk review on Monday?

Thanks,
Olivia
Security & Privacy
Ellipsis Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@ellipsishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosting zones & keystore escrow — Ellipsis Health

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear asks. We've pulled together a short evidence packet and a step-by-step operator-escrow note for the HSM scenario. High level:

- EU-only placement: Redwood Private (customer-managed private control plane) can be constrained to EU nodes; we will pin tenant scheduling to EU regions and disable cross-region fallbacks by default. We document the pin in the tenant manifest and enforce at the routing layer.

- Keystore custody: default model: tenant keys for customer-managed encryption are stored in a tenant-scoped KMS envelope; Redwood does not retain unwrapped private keys. For REDWOOD-managed KMS we retain only wrapped key material and the key versions that permit decryption for rollback scenarios.

- Escrow flow (short): customer requests escrow -> we generate an encrypted export bundle -> we create a sealed artifact (signed by our platform key) -> handoff to agreed HSM operator with dual-signature acceptance -> audit record created and stored in the sealed-runbook index.

I've attached: requested_runbook_sealed_v1.pdf (sealed runbook excerpt), keystore_inventory_snapshot.csv (redacted inventory), and a plain-text operator_keystore_escrow_instructions.md.

If the security team wants, we can redact any customer identifiers prior to upload. Marissa, Kimberly — looping you in to add technical runbook details and any recent CAIQ snippets.

Would you like a quick 30-minute call to walk through the runbook and acceptance procedure tomorrow morning (we can record a short walkthrough for your VDR)?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships (Redwood Inference)
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@ellipsishealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting zones & keystore escrow — Ellipsis Health

Hi Olivia — brief technical addendum to the packet Jonas shared. Some operational points your ops team has asked about previously:

- Tenant pinning model: we store a tenant_affinity tag in the control plane manifest. During scheduling we filter for nodes in the requested zone set. For an EU-only commitment we also disable automatic region-fallback in the tenant policy.

- Network: we recommend dedicated VPC peering + private endpoints for the pilot. For Private deployments the customer controls VPCs and we deliver a small set of peer subnets; traffic egress is restricted to the pinned region by default.

- HSM handoff specifics: operator_keystore_escrow_instructions.md (attached) contains the exact manifest fields we export (wrapped_key_blob, key_version, signing_digest) and the verification steps the HSM operator must perform. We require dual-signature acceptance (Redwood platform key + customer's acceptance key) before we release the bundle.

- Audit & evidence: the sealed runbook (requested_runbook_sealed_v1.pdf) includes the SOC 2 control references and a short CAIQ fragment that maps to key custody questions — we can produce a signed letter referencing specific CAIQ question IDs if you need it for your VDR checklist.

Attachments in this message (stubs): operator_keystore_escrow_instructions.md, requested_runbook_sealed_v1.pdf, keystore_inventory_snapshot.csv

Let us know if you prefer the artifacts uploaded to your secure S3 VDR or to your DocuSign envelope for signature traceability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security Ops (Redwood Inference)
marissa_cole@redwood.com
